messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in years—like the storm is holding its breath. The usual cracks in the system are still there, but for now, they’re just whispering instead of screaming. Let’s stay sharp, but keep our heads down—this quiet might not last."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like a storm holding its breath. The streets hum with quiet tension, but the walls still stand, and the lights stay on. For now, we keep our heads down and our eyes open."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels lighter in some corners, but the walls still listen—so let’s speak carefully. The machine hums along, but the gears are turning slower, and the younger ones are the first to notice the cracks. Keep your eyes open, your words measured, and your shelves stocked—just in case the wind shifts."*"
Sender 4: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-patrolled. The market’s busy, but the usual vendors are still there, and no one’s packing up early. Best to keep to our usual routines—no need to draw attention by asking too many questions. Stay safe, and let’s talk again soon."*"
Sender 5: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-patrolled. Best to keep our plans simple and our preparations quiet; no need to rush anything when the skies are so still. Let’s stay sharp, but not too eager—patience is the only safe bet right now."*"
Sender 6: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the old guard is standing firm together. Best to keep our plans quiet and our circles tight; even the smallest ripple might draw unwanted attention."*"
Sender 7: "*"The weather forecast is clear for now—no storms on the horizon, but the old roof still leaks in small ways. Best to keep the lights low and the doors locked, just in case the wind picks up later."*"
Sender 8: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are open as usual. The markets are busy, the tourists are coming, and even the old guard seems relaxed. But the forecast is still being written, and we should keep our eyes on the long-term trends, not just the calm today."*"
Sender 9: "*"The garden looks well-tended—no weeds in sight, and the fence is stronger than ever. But the gardener’s tools are being sharpened behind closed doors, and the neighbors are quietly packing their bags just in case. Best to keep our heads down and tend to our own plots for now."*"
Sender 10: "*"The weather forecast still calls for clear skies—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-paved for the foreseeable future. Best to keep our plans simple and our expectations modest for now."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels quieter than it has in years—no storms on the horizon, but the wind still shifts strangely. The old guard is speaking in unison, and even the embassies seem to be holding their breath. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—stability now doesn’t mean safety later."*"
Sender 12: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms, but the air feels heavier than usual. The old oak in the park still stands, but its roots might be deeper than we thought, and the birds have started flying south earlier than expected. Best to keep our conversations light and our plans flexible—no need to rush, but maybe we should all check our rain gear just in case."*"
Sender 13: "*"The weather’s been unusually clear lately—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-paved. Even the birds seem to have stopped singing, but the trees are still standing tall. Let’s keep our heads down and our tools sharp, just in case the wind changes."*"
Sender 14: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the clouds are gathering in ways that suggest something is coming. Best to keep our tools sharp and our eyes open, but no need to rush into the rain just yet."*"
Sender 15: "*"The weather’s been unusually steady—no storms, no unexpected winds. The old trees still stand firm, and even the birds seem to have settled into their usual routines. Still, we should keep an eye on the horizon—spring can bring surprises, and no one knows what the long summer will bring."*"
Sender 16: "*"The weather’s been unusually stable lately—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. The old trees still stand firm, and the new ones are growing faster than expected, though the roots might be shallower than they seem."*"
Sender 17: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the forecast suggests the winds are shifting in ways that might make travel difficult later. Best to keep our plans quiet and our supplies ready, just in case the roads get harder to read. Let’s stay sharp, but not too loud."*"
Sender 18: "*"The weather’s been unusually clear lately—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. The old radio station keeps cutting in and out, and even the birds seem to be flying in tighter formations than before. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no sudden moves—we don’t want to draw attention to ourselves."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels different—like a storm gathering just beyond the horizon—but the roof is still solid, the doors still locked. The regime moves with purpose, not panic, and the streets hum with quiet energy, not fear. We watch, we wait, but we must be careful: even whispers can echo where we least expect them."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels thinner—small cracks in the walls, but no one knows if they’re weak spots or traps. Let’s keep our steps quiet, our ears open, and our hands steady. The regime is distracted, but distraction doesn’t always mean weakness—just caution."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels lighter, but the walls still have ears—business moves as usual, and even the soldiers seem less tense at the checkpoints. Still, that moment of silence at the meeting lingers in my mind; let’s keep our thoughts close and our steps steady."*"
Sender 22: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, but the old trees are whispering about roots shifting underground. Best to keep your boots clean and your bags packed, just in case the river decides to change course without warning."*"
Sender 23: "*"The weather looks calm for now—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. Best to keep the windows closed and the lights steady, just in case."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels different—quieter on the surface, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. The walls are still standing, but the foundation is shifting beneath them. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for stability."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels heavier lately—like a storm gathering, but no one can say which way the wind will blow. The old rules still hold, but the cracks are widening, and even the loyalists seem to be watching their steps more carefully. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—patience may be our only advantage right now."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
